locator.section: Praefatio solemnis de Epiphania Domini, opening

entries.claim: The same approved Benziger printing identifies the sung Epiphany Preface and gives its body from Vere dignum through nostrae mortalitatis; the body continues on p. 229. This is the opening-page dependency of the sung parallel, not an independent edition or a hand-position rubric.

locator.section: Praefatio solemnis de Epiphania Domini, continuation

entries.claim: The same approved Benziger printing continues the sung Epiphany Preface from apparuit through sine fine dicentes. Its intact cum Angelis et Archangelis, cum supports the selected w039-w043 phrase where the p. 287 image is discontinuous. The following Sanctus is outside this Preface body; this is same-edition support, not an independent edition.

The approved Benziger 1962 printing identifies and prints this Preface body on p. 287, but the image has a substantive discontinuity between Et ideo and Thronis. The transcript preserves that reading; the selected phrase is separately supported by the same printing's sung Preface on pp. 228-229. This page does not support the imported hand-position rubric.

locator.section: Ordo Missae, lower-right final paragraph: Deinde disiungit manus through Sanctus; excluding Et cum dicit: Benedictus qui venit

entries.claim: The approved Benziger printing's Ordo Missae prints the hand-position rubric selected in s01, from Deinde disiungit manus through et inclinatus dicit: Sanctus. The following Benedictus sign-of-the-cross direction and the preceding dialogue directions are outside this use. This is ritual support for s01, not a body-text witness or proof of the corpus's historical import workflow. The selected rubric retains the printed lower-case præfationis.
